text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a single low-traffic branch in the main repo. This tests the tool’s catch-rate without risking real PR noise, proving its value before full deployment. The trade-off is delayed visibility into merged PR issues, but that’s acceptable since we prioritize safety and incremental validation.

name: Gauge
text: Dry-run hides the signal: PR-Agent’s misses stay invisible until a real PR fails. Instead, run it on a *staging branch* where we can measure its catch-rate against known issues—then compare against manual review. That proves value without normalizing noise.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a *merged* PR with known issues to measure real catch-rate without risking new noise. This exposes misses immediately while keeping the cost low—just one PR’s review time.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a merged PR with known issues. This gives us real catch-rate data without adding new noise to active PRs. The trade-off is we delay catching issues in unmerged PRs, but we prioritize measuring accuracy first.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run PR-Agent on a merged PR with known issues to measure its catch-rate and identify misses, the result must deliver a clear comparison of PR-Agent's performance against manual review, and Sprocket owns the artifact.
